title: Decision-Making in Agent-Based Models of Migration: State of the Art and Challenges

key_points.claim: Review scope: ABMs of human migration, examined by their agent decision-making rules.
key_points.evidence_quote: We review agent-based models (ABM) of human migration with respect to their decision-making rules.

key_points.claim: The dominant behavioural theories used as agent decision rules are random utility theory (discrete choice models) and the theory of planned behaviour.
key_points.evidence_quote: The most prominent behavioural theories used as decision rules are the random utility theory, as implemented in the discrete choice model, and the theory of planned behaviour.

key_points.claim: Two critical modelling choices are how decision processes and social networks are modelled.
key_points.evidence_quote: the critical choices that must be made in developing an ABM, namely the modelling of decision processes and social networks

key_points.claim: Two challenges hinder wider ABM use in demography and the social sciences: operationalising a behavioural theory, and choosing empirical evidence for validation.
key_points.evidence_quote: (a) the choice and the operationalisation of a behavioural theory (decision-making and social interaction) and (b) the selection of empirical evidence to validate the model.

reliability_notes: Abstract only was checked. The fetch returned the full page, but I ran out of tool calls before reading the body text. Peer-reviewed review by Frans Willekens (Max Planck Institute for Demographic Research), open access. The body text likely contains more detail that these notes don't cover.
